title: What if the Sun went dark for one full day?

lines.text: What would happen if the Sun completely turned off for twenty-four hours?
lines.caps: What if the Sun | turned *black | for *24 hours?

lines.text: Because sunlight takes eight minutes to reach us, nobody on Earth would notice a thing for the first eight minutes.
lines.caps: We wouldn't notice | for the *first | eight *minutes

lines.text: Then, pitch black darkness would engulf the daytime hemisphere in a terrifying instant.
Global temperatures would drop noticeably by ten to fifteen degrees, frosting windshields everywhere.
lines.caps: Temperatures plummet | as *freezing cold | creeps in

lines.text: Photosynthesis would pause and birds would frantically roost thinking night arrived early.
lines.caps: Plants pause *growth | and wildlife falls | into *panic

lines.text: Yet because Earth's thick atmosphere retains geothermal heat, humanity would survive the short blackout.
lines.caps: Earth retains enough *heat | to survive | one day

lines.text: When the blazing light burst back twenty-four hours later, it would be the most celebrated sunrise in history.
lines.caps: The next *sunrise | would be the greatest | *celebration!
